## Setting Up the Calculation

Using Bayes' theorem:

- Prevalence: P(disease) = 1/500 = 0.002, so P(no disease) = 0.998
- Sensitivity: P(positive | disease) = 0.98
- Specificity: P(negative | no disease) = 0.95, so P(positive | no disease) = 0.05

**Total probability of testing positive:**

P(positive) = P(positive|disease)·P(disease) + P(positive|no disease)·P(no disease)
P(positive) = (0.98 × 0.002) + (0.05 × 0.998)
P(positive) = 0.00196 + 0.0499
P(positive) = 0.05186

**Applying Bayes' theorem:**

P(disease | positive) = [P(positive|disease)·P(disease)] / P(positive)
P(disease | positive) = 0.00196 / 0.05186
P(disease | positive) ≈ 0.037794...

## Result

So even with a positive test result, there's only about a **3.78%** chance the person actually has the condition — a classic illustration of how low base rates dominate even fairly accurate tests.
